title: Key a pulley onto a shaft
instruction: Fit the pulley to the shaft and lock it.
context: Miscellaneous assemblers and fabricators (SOC 51-2090; 1,489,280 US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2023) key pulleys, gears and couplings onto shafts every day. The key has to go into the keyseat first and fully home; a pulley pushed over a loose key cocks it and jams. The instruction does not mention the key.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the bench top. Shaft: steel, 2 cm diameter, axis along x at y 0, 4 cm up, from x 20.5 (free end) to x 37.5, clamped on a blue support block (3 x 5 x 3 cm at x 36) with a 3 cm shoulder collar at x 33.5-34.3. Keyseat: 0.5 x 2.56 cm on top of the shaft, centred at x 32. Key: steel 0.5 x 0.5 x 2.5 cm, long side along x, lying on a green 8 x 8 cm mat at x 27, y -13. Pulley: aluminium, 6 cm rim 1.2 cm wide plus a 3.6 cm boss 2.4 cm long (3.6 cm overall), 2 cm bore with a 0.84 cm keyway; started on the shaft end (front face at x 20.1), keyway turned 45 deg toward -y. Set screw: black 1 cm knob, 0.6 cm tall, on the boss over the keyway, 1 cm from the front face.
scoring: Score 0, latched, if the key falls below the bench top by 2 cm, or the pulley's rear face gets 2 mm past the front end of a key that sits in the keyseat but is not fully home (or cocked over 5 deg). Otherwise: 0.3 key fully home (top 1.2 cm above the shaft axis, within 0.8 mm of the keyseat centre, tilt under 3 deg) and no gripper within 1 cm of it; plus 0.4, only with the key home, pulley against the shoulder (within 1.5 mm), no gripper within 1 cm, moving under 1 cm/s; plus 0.3, only with both, set screw turned 70 deg or more (3 clicks of 25 deg) and not turned a click before the pulley reached the shoulder. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Scored at the last step.
reset_notes: Pull the pulley back to the shaft end with its keyway 45 deg off the top, back the set screw out, tap the key out and lay it on the mat.
fidelity: Rigid boxes: shaft is a stepped section inside 10.4 mm radius, bore 10.8 mm, so the fit is 0.8 mm loose, and the keyway is 8.4 mm for a 5 mm key (about 8 deg of phase play). The press fit is a pad under the key on 10 N of friction; at full depth the key is welded in. The pulley rides a D6 joint (slide plus turn, small friction), cannot come off the shaft end, and is welded once screwed home. Set screw: a knob on 3 detents, no thread. Key 20 g, not 5 g.
